items.content:
Given the rumor that Venezuela is considering an exit from OPEC, it is worth mentioning that I was the inspiration behind the UAE’s exit from OPEC.

While serving on the UAE’s Financial Advisory Council from 2008 to 2014, I developed an optimum depletion rate model for in situ resources, like oil, plugged in realistic numbers, and concluded that the UAE should be depleting its vast oil reserves at a much more rapid rate than it was.

The logic is simple: if you think the real price of oil will fall, or that future barrels will not be available for pumping or delivery, you are incentivized to tilt production away from the future and toward the present.

In short, you should TAKE THE MONEY AND RUN.

My simple model for the economics of depletable resources is contained in an RIP I wrote for one of my mentors, Prof. M.A. "Morry" Adelman of MIT, perhaps the greatest petroleum economist of all time.
